newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ANYKSCHIU SAYS SITUATION "NOT SO GOOD".
newsitem.headline: ANYKSCHIU SAYS SITUATION "NOT SO GOOD".

text.p: Wine producer and bottler Anykschiu Wine, owned 84 percent by the state, on Tuesday said that its situation was not healthy although its 1996 profits showed a rise.
"Our net profit looks impresive on paper but in reality the situation is not that good," the director of Anykschiu Wine Jonas Makshtele told Reuters.
He declined to forecast the company's net profit for 1997.
The company earlier announced a 1996 net profit of 13.4 million litas, versus 7.2 million litas a year earlier.
He said that Anykschiu municipality owed the company around six million litas for heat which the company's heating facilities provide to the city's inhabitants, Makshtele said.
He also said that company's clients owe another two million litas and it is unlikely that Anykschiu Wine will regain the money because of complicated court procedures.
The government has not included Anykschiu Wine on the privatisation list so far as the company was banned from sale by the previous government.
Anykschiu Wine is listed in the group A of Vilnius bourse and its market price today was 1.36 litas.
